settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: LabradorRetriever.read throws IllegalStateException for 'text/html' content type, mitigating the common 'login page returned instead of data' scenario.
TransportFormat.XML path (readFromXml) is used when Content-Type is 'text/xml', avoiding native deserialization in that case.

No evidence in the reviewed source that an unauthenticated external HTTP client can directly reach readSerializableFrom (it is used for outbound collector->agent calls), so exploitation requires a malicious/compromised monitored endpoint or network position.
candidates.description: TransportFormat.readSerializableFrom() for the SERIALIZED format wraps the incoming stream in a plain java.io.ObjectInputStream and calls readObject() with no ObjectInputFilter or whitelist. LabradorRetriever.read() invokes transportFormat.readSerializableFrom(input) on data received over an HTTP connection to a monitored-application URL, and defaults to TransportFormat.SERIALIZED unless the Content-Type starts with 'text/xml' (Content-Type 'text/html' throws). The URL is supplied via the collector application configuration (application URLs are user/administrator-provided, e.g. via CollectorServlet doPost appUrls / CollectorController.addCollectorApplication). If any configured monitoring URL points at a host that is not fully trusted (or is compromised / subject to MITM / returns arbitrary bytes), the collector will natively deserialize attacker-controlled Java objects, enabling gadget-chain code execution under the CollectorServer process. The default-branch fallback to SERIALIZED (lines 296-300) widens exposure, since any non-XML, non-HTML content type is treated as a Java serialized stream.
missing_evidence: Deployment guidance that monitored URLs are always fully trusted and that native SERIALIZED format is the documented default.
Any ObjectInputFilter / JEP-290 style allow-list applied elsewhere before deserialization.
Whether serialization classes present on the classpath contain known gadget chains usable at runtime.
preconditions: Collector (CollectorServer) configured with one or more monitored-application URLs (Parameters.parseUrl / addCollectorApplication).
A monitored URL is attacker-influenced, compromised, or reachable over a channel allowing response substitution (no TLS, or MITM).
Response stream returned to the collector is not the expected serialized type but arbitrary Java serialization bytes (or the content type is crafted to reach the default SERIALIZED branch).
candidates.title: Java native deserialization of untrusted collector responses (ObjectInputStream on remote host data)

counter_evidence: createXStream() registers aliases only; it does not explicitly open arbitrary classes, though XStream's default behavior still permits many types absent a security framework.
JSON format explicitly disables deserialization (throws UnsupportedOperationException) in readSerializableFrom.
No source evidence that untrusted external clients can drive this directly; it is tied to the outbound collector->agent fetch path.
candidates.description: TransportFormat.XmlIO.readFromXml() creates an XStream instance via createXStream(false) and calls xstream.fromXML(reader) on the buffered input stream without configuring any XStream security framework (no allowlist / XStream.setupDefaultSecurity / forbid types). createXStream() only registers aliases and two local MapConverters; a MapConverter with canConvert() returning true is also registered. LabradorRetriever selects TransportFormat.XML when the remote response Content-Type starts with 'text/xml' and then deserializes with XStream. If a monitored endpoint (or a network attacker able to control the response content type/body) returns crafted XML, XStream can be induced to instantiate arbitrary types present on the classpath, a well-known RCE vector when unrestricted. The bundled XStream version in the dependency declarations is 1.4.2/1.3.1, which predates the hardened default security of later releases.
missing_evidence: Whether a global XStream security configuration or type allowlist is applied elsewhere at runtime.
Exact effective XStream version resolved at runtime and its default security posture.
Whether any deployment-enforced authentication/data-integrity protects the monitored endpoints' responses.
preconditions: Collector configured with monitored URLs (same as the SERIALIZED-format candidate).
Remote response Content-Type advertised or set as 'text/xml' (or path chosen by attacker) so that TransportFormat.XML is selected.
Classpath contains XStream and any gadget-capable types reachable by XStream.
candidates.title: XStream XML deserialization of untrusted collector responses without type/security restrictions

counter_evidence: isAddressNotAllowed enforces a positive allow-list when ALLOWED_ADDR_PATTERN is set, which is the intended hardening.
Action.checkSystemActionsEnabled() gates several sensitive 'part' actions, implying system-actions enabled/disabled configuration exists.
Deployment web.xml / container realm may add authentication; the reviewed Java sources do not implement authentication, so it may be supplied externally.
candidates.description: CollectorServlet.init() compiles allowedAddrPattern only if Parameters.getParameter(Parameter.ALLOWED_ADDR_PATTERN) is non-null; isAddressNotAllowed() returns false (access allowed) whenever allowedAddrPattern == null. Thus, absent configuration, any network client reaching the collector servlet is permitted. doGet/doPost then route to CollectorController, which exposes system actions gated only by Action.checkSystemActionsEnabled() (SESSIONS, HEAP_HISTO, JNDI, PROCESSES, MBEANS, DATABASE, CONNECTIONS, HOTSPOTS) and actions that proxy requests to monitored applications (forwardActionAndUpdateData, doProxy with part=web.xml / pom.xml). This means the security of the collector relies entirely on the operator setting ALLOWED_ADDR_PATTERN plus any container-level authentication declared in web.xml; the code itself provides no mandatory authentication or CSRF protection for these state-changing/privileged operations (e.g., remove_application, adding applications via doPost).
missing_evidence: The collector-webapp web.xml content governing servlet URL mappings and any declared security-constraint/login-config.
Whether system-actions are disabled by default and how Action.checkSystemActionsEnabled is configured.
Whether CSRF protections exist for the add/remove application POST flows elsewhere not yet reviewed.
preconditions: Collector webapp deployed with the collector servlet reachable by network clients.
ALLOWED_ADDR_PATTERN not configured (or pattern too permissive), and no external authentication/authorization wrapper in front of the servlet.
Attacker has network reachability to the collector servlet context path.
candidates.title: Collector servlet access control is default-open when allowed-addr-pattern is not configured
